text.p: Energis, the fledgling fixed line telecoms group owned by the National Grid Group Plc, confirmed on Monday that it was in talks with UK mobile telephone leader Vodafone Group Plc about offering joint customer services.

"The aim would be for Vodafone to be able to offer Energis' fixed line services to the Vodafone business customer base and, potentially, for Energis to be able to market Vodafone mobile services to the Energis business customers base," the company said in a brief statement.
An Energis spokeswoman said she expected a marketing agreement, which would strengthen both companies' services to business customers, to be completed in around one month.

Amid increasing convergence between fixed and mobile telecoms operators, Energis has already sealed an interconnect agreement with Vodafone and also carries traffic over its fibre-optic network from Vodafone's cellular rival Orange Plc .
But this is the first time a mobile telephone company will be offering fixed services to its business customers in Britain.

While mobile telephone companies attempt to hang onto high-margin business customers, Energis says there is growing demand for integrated mobile services, which bring with them customer benefits such as single bills.

Eyes will now turn to fixed line telecoms giants British Telecommunications Plc and Cable and Wireless Communications, to see whether they will attempt to follow suit and integrate services from their two cellular relations -- Cellnet and One2One.

BT might use the latest Vodafone deal to try and convince industry regulator Oftel to lift a restriction on it from buying the 40 percent of Cellnet it does not already own so it too can offer a similar package.
One2One, which is jointly owned by CWC's parent Cable and Wireless Plc and U S West Inc, said in May that it was not in talks about joining Cable and Wireless Communications.
